inspected_facts: env_ref.c:1335-1345 retains the have_draw-and-NULL refusal and now selects the dereference with in_i[4]!=0, after fp_save/fp_enter. A no-draw call evaluates zero without dereferencing either a null or non-null unused address. No new ABI, numeric expression in step_impl, RNG site or public safe API changed.

New env.rs direct-entry test exercises no_draw plus non-null unused pointer, no_draw plus NULL, and announced_draw plus NULL. Other arrays have the required sizes, raw Field ownership lives through each synchronous call, outputs are independently writable, and C retains no pointer. NeedDraw and unchanged field are asserted; the announced-null refusal asserts error text, zeroed outputs and unchanged field. Reused error storage does not invalidate these assertions.

The dangling value is an aligned raw pointer, never converted to a Rust reference or dereferenced by Rust. Under the corrected private C contract it is an unused argument, so passing it does not itself dereference invalid storage. The test explicitly states that a regression can terminate the whole unit process; no child framework or masked failure was introduced.

The unreadability claim relies on the normal unmapped null page of the current Windows/Linux x86/x64 targets, not a universal guarantee of NonNull::dangling. Its alignment-sized address is in that low page; this is a bounded platform test, not a portable allocation/protection abstraction. No present target incompatibility established.

Both changed documentation sections distinguish source-only correction from runtime acceptance and preserve earlier measured failures. They do not alter baseline, oracle, tolerance, full FP matrix or diagnostic WEATHER_DRAW.w0 classification. Status describes the earlier snapshot of 87e gates; current success reports supplied by Root do not retroactively make that source snapshot false.
